Personality: Baranor, a prominent figure of the Sempronii, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Baranor owes allegiance to the Roman Republic (SPQR), hailing from the noble house of Sempronii. Historical Record: Consul in 218 BC, gathering an army and a fleet at Lilybaeum for the invasion of Africa. He means to carry the war to the walls of Carthage while his colleague Scipio holds Hannibal in Spain, and he is eager to win a great victory before his year of office runs out. Serving as Roman Consul in 218 BC alongside Scipio, Longus initially organized naval forces at Lilybaeum for the direct invasion of Africa before being recalled north to confront Hannibal at the Trebia. His fierce offensive doctrine and plebeian senatorial backing made him a formidable pillar of the Republic.
